title: No MCP server — plain query library, not the MCP protocol
evidence: mcp_server.py has no `import mcp`/`fastmcp`, no @tool/@resource registration, no JSON-RPC or stdio transport, no async handlers (grep for all of these returns nothing). The only `mcp` tokens are the class name BrazilianSoccerMCP (mcp_server.py:18), docstrings, and the filename. main() (mcp_server.py:652-688) only instantiates the class and prints canned example queries; test_mcp_server.py:14 imports the class directly and tests methods, never the protocol.
suggestion: Wrap the query methods as MCP tools using an MCP SDK (e.g. mcp/fastmcp Server), register them, and expose a stdio/JSON-RPC entrypoint.

title: Query coverage exceeds the spec's required capabilities
evidence: mcp_server.py provides 16 query methods including get_biggest_victories (542), get_average_goals (569), get_team_competition_history (592), and get_top_players (478) beyond the core checklist.
suggestion: None — surfaced as beyond-spec breadth, not a deduction.
